claims.text: Dynamic loading of HEAs induces nano twins at pre-existing low-angle grain boundaries, enhancing dynamic mechanical behavior.
Deformation-induced nano twins promote localized dislocation avalanches.
Nano twins and dislocation avalanches jointly improve the balance between strength and ductility.
Relevant HEAs can be single- or dual-phase solid solutions.
HEAs have complex, approximately equiatomic compositions.
Atomic-size mismatch in compositionally complex HEAs produces lattice distortion that affects defect activity and mechanical properties.
Rapid non-equilibrium processing produces HEAs with a significant fraction of low-angle grain boundaries.
Room-temperature or cryogenic high-strain-rate or cyclic loading can activate both dislocation avalanches and nano-twin formation.
Low-angle grain boundaries serve as nucleation sites for nano twins during dynamic loading.
Rapid non-equilibrium processing creates the low-angle-grain-boundary-rich microstructure required for the proposed mechanism.
The nano twins accommodate plastic deformation through localized dislocation avalanches.
Twin-mediated deformation enhances ductility without compromising strength.
Slow equilibrium cooling yields fewer low-angle grain boundaries and minimal deformation-induced nano twinning relative to rapid processing.
Rapidly processed HEAs will have greater ductility than slowly cooled HEAs under otherwise identical dynamic loading.
Stepwise stress-strain changes are signatures of dislocation-avalanche behavior.
The stepwise stress-strain changes will correlate with a higher post-loading nano-twin density.
The mechanism is restricted to compositionally complex, lattice-distorted HEAs processed so as to retain abundant low-angle grain boundaries.
The magnitude of the nano-twin and avalanche contribution relative to ordinary dislocation motion and phase-boundary effects has not been quantitatively established.
Rapid solidification is expected to create both a high density of low-angle grain boundaries and nano twins before the loading comparison.
Failure of the rapid-processing condition to produce higher nano-twin density, avalanche signatures, and ductility than the slow-cooling control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes nano twins as deformation-induced during loading, whereas the experimental design says rapid solidification itself is expected to create the nano twins. This makes their pre-loading versus loading-induced status inconsistent.
